{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 925,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "History and Origin can panic when search is not configured",
      "body": "`server.History` calls `s.search.History(...)` and `server.Origin` calls `s.search.Origin(...)` without checking whether `s.search` is nil. `NewResourceServer` can leave `s.search` nil when search resources are not configured or when `SearchOptions.Backend` is nil (`newSearchSupport` returns nil, nil). A gRPC History or Origin request in that configuration will dereference a nil pointer and panic. `Search` has a nil guard, but History and Origin do not."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 190,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Startup index-build goroutines share and race on the outer err variable",
      "body": "In `searchSupport.init`, each errgroup closure assigns to the outer `err` variable via `_, _, err = s.build(...)` and then returns it. Multiple index-build goroutines run concurrently and write to the same variable, causing a data race. This can also cause one goroutine's error to be overwritten by another goroutine's success, so `Init` may report success even though an index build failed. Each closure should use its own local error variable."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 189,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Unsynchronized increment of totalBatchesIndexed in concurrent startup builds",
      "body": "`totalBatchesIndexed++` is executed inside errgroup goroutines without any synchronization. Multiple goroutines can increment the same integer concurrently, which is a data race and can produce an incorrect value in the `namespaced_indexed` span attribute. Use an atomic counter or protect the counter with a mutex."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 203,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Events written during initial index build can be missed permanently",
      "body": "`searchSupport.init` builds all initial indexes first and only afterward calls `WatchWriteEvents` to start consuming new events. The resource version returned by `build`/`ListIterator` is discarded. Any writes committed between the initial listing for a namespace and the creation of the watch subscription are not applied to the newly built index. Because startup indexing can take a long time, this creates a potentially large window where the search index can become stale until another write happens for the same resource."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 209,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Search event loop does not handle a closed watch channel",
      "body": "The event loop started by `searchSupport.init` receives from the watch channel with `v := <-events` and does not check whether the channel is closed. The SQL backend closes its event channel on shutdown. After closure, this loop receives nil repeatedly and calls `handleEvent` with a nil event, causing a nil-pointer dereference on `evt.Type` or a tight loop. The loop also uses `context.Background()` and has no graceful shutdown path."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 762,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Broadcaster pipe does not handle a closed backend event channel",
      "body": "In `server.initWatcher`, the goroutine that pipes backend watch events reads `v := <-events` without checking the channel's ok value and then accesses `v.Type` and `v.ResourceVersion`. If the backend closes the event channel, as the SQL backend does when stopped, this dereferences a nil event and panics, or spins on a closed channel. A closed-channel check and shutdown path are needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 72,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "BuildIndex no longer serializes builds for the same index key",
      "body": "`bleveBackend.BuildIndex` now performs the full index build without holding `cacheMu` or any per-key lock, and only locks briefly to write the cache. Concurrent calls for the same `NamespacedResource` can both observe no cached index from `GetIndex` and then build indexes simultaneously. This can create duplicate indexes, overwrite the cache without closing the previous index, and for file-based indexes can attempt to open/build the same directory concurrently, causing errors or corruption. A per-key lock, singleflight mechanism, or cache re-check under lock is needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 146,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "TotalDocs iterates the index cache without locking",
      "body": "`bleveBackend.TotalDocs` iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `cacheMu`, while `BuildIndex` writes to the same map under the lock. Concurrent calls to `TotalDocs` and index builds can cause a concurrent map read/write race, which can crash the process."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 258,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Constructor leaks resources when Init fails",
      "body": "`NewResourceServer` creates a cancelable context and then calls `s.Init(ctx)`. If `Init` fails, the constructor returns an error without calling the cancel function and without stopping any components that were partially initialized. If lifecycle initialization succeeded, or if `search.init` started its event goroutine before a later watcher failure, those resources and goroutines are leaked on construction failure."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 263,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "handleEvent can panic when IndexMetrics is nil",
      "body": "`searchSupport.handleEvent` uses `IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds` for ADDED and DELETED events without checking whether `IndexMetrics` is nil. Other code paths guard this global with `if IndexMetrics != nil`. If metrics are not initialized, processing a watch event will panic."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 102,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "BuildIndex can panic when IndexMetrics is nil",
      "body": "`bleveBackend.BuildIndex` increments `resource.IndexMetrics.IndexTenants` without checking whether `resource.IndexMetrics` is nil. Other parts of the code guard this global, so building an index can panic when metrics are not initialized."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 461,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "builderCache.get can return a nil DocumentBuilder without error",
      "body": "`builderCache.get` falls back to `s.defaultBuilder` and returns it without error. `newBuilderCache` does not require a default builder unless the configuration list is empty, so for an unregistered group/resource this can return a nil `DocumentBuilder` with a nil error. Callers such as `searchSupport.build` and `searchSupport.handleEvent` then call `BuildDocument` on the nil builder and panic."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 128,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Bleve index is not closed when BuildIndex fails after creation",
      "body": "In `bleveBackend.BuildIndex`, if `getAllFields` or the builder callback fails after `bleve.New` or `bleve.NewMemOnly` has created an index, the function returns without closing the newly created `bleve.Index`. For file-backed indexes this leaks file handles and can leave a locked index directory behind."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go",
      "line": 586,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Poller span is not ended when listLatestRVs fails",
      "body": "In `backend.poller`, a span is started on every poll tick. If `listLatestRVs` returns an error, the code resets the ticker and continues without calling `span.End()`. Repeated failures will leak spans and retain tracing state unnecessarily."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/server/module_server_test.go",
      "line": 36,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Postgres coverage is skipped for storage server startup test",
      "body": "The integration test now skips all Postgres runs. Since this PR changes startup initialization and indexing behavior, Postgres coverage for the storage server target is lost, and the failure mode that motivated the skip is only annotated with a TODO."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: History and Origin can panic when search is not configured
findings.body: `server.History` calls `s.search.History(...)` and `server.Origin` calls `s.search.Origin(...)` without checking whether `s.search` is nil. `NewResourceServer` can leave `s.search` nil when search resources are not configured or when `SearchOptions.Backend` is nil (`newSearchSupport` returns nil, nil). A gRPC History or Origin request in that configuration will dereference a nil pointer and panic. `Search` has a nil guard, but History and Origin do not.

findings.title: Startup index-build goroutines share and race on the outer err variable
findings.body: In `searchSupport.init`, each errgroup closure assigns to the outer `err` variable via `_, _, err = s.build(...)` and then returns it. Multiple index-build goroutines run concurrently and write to the same variable, causing a data race. This can also cause one goroutine's error to be overwritten by another goroutine's success, so `Init` may report success even though an index build failed. Each closure should use its own local error variable.

findings.title: Unsynchronized increment of totalBatchesIndexed in concurrent startup builds
findings.body: `totalBatchesIndexed++` is executed inside errgroup goroutines without any synchronization. Multiple goroutines can increment the same integer concurrently, which is a data race and can produce an incorrect value in the `namespaced_indexed` span attribute. Use an atomic counter or protect the counter with a mutex.

findings.title: Events written during initial index build can be missed permanently
findings.body: `searchSupport.init` builds all initial indexes first and only afterward calls `WatchWriteEvents` to start consuming new events. The resource version returned by `build`/`ListIterator` is discarded. Any writes committed between the initial listing for a namespace and the creation of the watch subscription are not applied to the newly built index. Because startup indexing can take a long time, this creates a potentially large window where the search index can become stale until another write happens for the same resource.

findings.title: Search event loop does not handle a closed watch channel
findings.body: The event loop started by `searchSupport.init` receives from the watch channel with `v := <-events` and does not check whether the channel is closed. The SQL backend closes its event channel on shutdown. After closure, this loop receives nil repeatedly and calls `handleEvent` with a nil event, causing a nil-pointer dereference on `evt.Type` or a tight loop. The loop also uses `context.Background()` and has no graceful shutdown path.

findings.title: Broadcaster pipe does not handle a closed backend event channel
findings.body: In `server.initWatcher`, the goroutine that pipes backend watch events reads `v := <-events` without checking the channel's ok value and then accesses `v.Type` and `v.ResourceVersion`. If the backend closes the event channel, as the SQL backend does when stopped, this dereferences a nil event and panics, or spins on a closed channel. A closed-channel check and shutdown path are needed.

findings.title: BuildIndex no longer serializes builds for the same index key
findings.body: `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` now performs the full index build without holding `cacheMu` or any per-key lock, and only locks briefly to write the cache. Concurrent calls for the same `NamespacedResource` can both observe no cached index from `GetIndex` and then build indexes simultaneously. This can create duplicate indexes, overwrite the cache without closing the previous index, and for file-based indexes can attempt to open/build the same directory concurrently, causing errors or corruption. A per-key lock, singleflight mechanism, or cache re-check under lock is needed.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without locking
findings.body: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `cacheMu`, while `BuildIndex` writes to the same map under the lock. Concurrent calls to `TotalDocs` and index builds can cause a concurrent map read/write race, which can crash the process.

findings.title: Constructor leaks resources when Init fails
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` creates a cancelable context and then calls `s.Init(ctx)`. If `Init` fails, the constructor returns an error without calling the cancel function and without stopping any components that were partially initialized. If lifecycle initialization succeeded, or if `search.init` started its event goroutine before a later watcher failure, those resources and goroutines are leaked on construction failure.

findings.title: handleEvent can panic when IndexMetrics is nil
findings.body: `searchSupport.handleEvent` uses `IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds` for ADDED and DELETED events without checking whether `IndexMetrics` is nil. Other code paths guard this global with `if IndexMetrics != nil`. If metrics are not initialized, processing a watch event will panic.

findings.title: BuildIndex can panic when IndexMetrics is nil
findings.body: `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` increments `resource.IndexMetrics.IndexTenants` without checking whether `resource.IndexMetrics` is nil. Other parts of the code guard this global, so building an index can panic when metrics are not initialized.

findings.title: builderCache.get can return a nil DocumentBuilder without error
findings.body: `builderCache.get` falls back to `s.defaultBuilder` and returns it without error. `newBuilderCache` does not require a default builder unless the configuration list is empty, so for an unregistered group/resource this can return a nil `DocumentBuilder` with a nil error. Callers such as `searchSupport.build` and `searchSupport.handleEvent` then call `BuildDocument` on the nil builder and panic.

findings.title: Bleve index is not closed when BuildIndex fails after creation
findings.body: In `bleveBackend.BuildIndex`, if `getAllFields` or the builder callback fails after `bleve.New` or `bleve.NewMemOnly` has created an index, the function returns without closing the newly created `bleve.Index`. For file-backed indexes this leaks file handles and can leave a locked index directory behind.

findings.title: Poller span is not ended when listLatestRVs fails
findings.body: In `backend.poller`, a span is started on every poll tick. If `listLatestRVs` returns an error, the code resets the ticker and continues without calling `span.End()`. Repeated failures will leak spans and retain tracing state unnecessarily.

findings.title: Postgres coverage is skipped for storage server startup test
findings.body: The integration test now skips all Postgres runs. Since this PR changes startup initialization and indexing behavior, Postgres coverage for the storage server target is lost, and the failure mode that motivated the skip is only annotated with a TODO.
